caution: Validate the measured values and proposed configuration below. Savings are scenarios, not invoice reductions. Change capacity in stages; check latency, queueing, spill, memory and workload requirements after each change. Missing activity is not proof that a resource is unused. Keep cloud infrastructure costs separate from Databricks costs.

cluster_autotermination.title: Enable or shorten cluster auto-termination
cluster_autotermination.why: Observed inactivity can keep cluster compute running and billed.
cluster_autotermination.how: In Compute, open the cluster and edit auto-termination. Use the proposed timeout below; confirm that interactive users can tolerate restarts.

warehouse_autostop.title: Enable or shorten SQL warehouse auto-stop
warehouse_autostop.why: The warehouse remains warm between queries. Reclaimable idle hours depend on restart overhead and observed gaps.
warehouse_autostop.how: In SQL Warehouses, edit Auto stop. Compare the timeout candidates and restart trade-off below before applying the proposed value.

warehouse_autostop_serverless.title: Shorten serverless warehouse auto-stop
warehouse_autostop_serverless.why: Idle intervals can be billed even on a serverless warehouse. The best timeout balances idle cost and query restarts.
warehouse_autostop_serverless.how: In SQL Warehouses, edit Auto stop using the measured gap distribution and proposed timeout. Check cold starts and user latency.

idle_zombie_clusters.title: Review idle clusters
idle_zombie_clusters.why: Observed CPU and activity indicate long idle periods, but bursts and recent use still matter.
idle_zombie_clusters.how: Inspect active days and the last activity below. Confirm ownership and dependencies before terminating the cluster or tightening auto-termination.

rightsize_underutilized.title: Right-size underutilized clusters
rightsize_underutilized.why: Measured CPU suggests capacity headroom. CPU alone does not prove that a smaller cluster will satisfy memory, IO and runtime requirements.
rightsize_underutilized.how: Compare current and proposed capacity below. Reduce one stage at a time, run representative workloads and check CPU, memory, spill and duration.

jobs_compute_rightsize.title: Right-size job compute
jobs_compute_rightsize.why: Driver/worker utilization can reveal idle workers, driver-bound execution or excess memory allocation.
jobs_compute_rightsize.how: Inspect the diagnosed bottleneck below. Test a smaller node, fewer workers or single-node execution as applicable; retain the configuration only if job SLAs hold.

enable_photon_dbr.title: Review Runtime and Photon
enable_photon_dbr.why: Older runtimes or disabled Photon may leave eligible SQL workloads running longer.
enable_photon_dbr.how: Benchmark a current LTS Runtime with Photon on representative work. Compare total DBU cost and duration before migrating.

enable_serverless.title: Evaluate SQL warehouse migration to Serverless
enable_serverless.why: Measured idle gaps can favor serverless, but a higher DBU rate and active runtime must be included in the comparison.
enable_serverless.how: Check compatibility, active/idle hours and price assumptions below. Test Serverless with the same workload. Treat cloud VM savings as a separate, estimated layer.

interactive_to_job.title: Move scheduled work off all-purpose clusters
interactive_to_job.why: Scheduled workloads may use a more expensive all-purpose compute rate. Shared-cluster spend disappears only if the source cluster can actually shrink or stop.
interactive_to_job.how: Move eligible tasks to dedicated job compute or serverless jobs. Verify runtime and dependencies, then confirm that the original cluster's billed capacity decreases.

cluster_job_contention.title: Isolate jobs competing on a shared cluster
cluster_job_contention.why: Overlapping jobs can compete for the same CPU and memory. Adding capacity does not remove coupling between jobs.
cluster_job_contention.how: Inspect overlap and saturation, then test dedicated job compute or serverless for each job. This advisory does not book a separate saving.

spot_fallback.title: Evaluate spot workers with fallback
spot_fallback.why: On-demand worker capacity may have a lower-cost spot alternative, subject to availability and interruption risk.
spot_fallback.how: In cluster availability settings, test SPOT_WITH_FALLBACK for workers and keep the driver on-demand. Validate retries, reliability and realized cloud prices.

serverless_cost_optimized.title: Evaluate cost-optimized serverless execution
serverless_cost_optimized.why: Performance-optimized startup can cost more for workloads that tolerate a slower start.
serverless_cost_optimized.how: For the job or pipeline, test Standard / cost-optimized performance. Check startup latency and end-to-end SLA before keeping the change.

failing_jobs.title: Fix or retire repeatedly failing jobs
failing_jobs.why: Repeated failures consume compute without completing intended work.
failing_jobs.how: Open failed job runs and inspect output and logs. Fix the root cause, review retries and alerts, or pause the schedule after confirming business ownership.

unused_data_jobs.title: Review jobs producing unread data
unused_data_jobs.why: Lineage shows no observed reads of the output. External readers and access outside the observation window may be invisible.
unused_data_jobs.how: Check downstream dashboards, external consumers and retention requirements. Pause or retire the job only after confirming that its output is unnecessary.

unused_scheduled_jobs.title: Review unused scheduled jobs
unused_scheduled_jobs.why: Scheduled execution may no longer correspond to an active business need.
unused_scheduled_jobs.how: Confirm the last successful run, dependencies and owner. Pause the schedule first; delete only after validating that the workload is no longer required.

warehouse_rightsize.title: Right-size an oversized SQL warehouse
warehouse_rightsize.why: Measured Spark slot occupancy, or weaker queue/spill proxies when slot data is missing, suggests headroom. A smaller size may lengthen queries or require more clusters.
warehouse_rightsize.how: Reduce one size step and monitor p95 runtime, queueing, spill and running cluster count. Use the measured floor as a staged target, not a single large jump.

warehouse_scale_out.title: Scale out a constrained SQL warehouse
warehouse_scale_out.why: Queries wait for capacity. This is a performance advisory, not a cost-saving action; additional clusters can increase busy-hour spend.
warehouse_scale_out.how: Review queueing and hourly concurrency. Test increasing max clusters by one while preserving auto-stop; compare latency and total spend.

idle_serving_endpoints.title: Review idle serving endpoints
idle_serving_endpoints.why: Measured request traffic indicates zero or low use. Low traffic is less certain than a directly observed zero-request interval.
idle_serving_endpoints.how: Confirm callers and availability needs. Where supported, enable scale-to-zero or reduce minimum capacity; delete only after confirming the endpoint is unnecessary.

gpu_wrong_runtime.title: Review GPU instances without a GPU Runtime
gpu_wrong_runtime.why: A GPU instance without a compatible GPU Runtime may pay for hardware the workload cannot use.
gpu_wrong_runtime.how: Check actual GPU requirements and libraries. Benchmark CPU instances, or use the correct GPU Runtime when acceleration is needed.

untagged_spend.title: Tag spend for chargeback
untagged_spend.why: Usage lacks the required allocation tags, making ownership and cost attribution difficult. Unattributable spend is not a saving.
untagged_spend.how: Apply the required tags through compute policies and job configuration. Confirm coverage in billing usage after the next refresh.

continuous_pipeline.title: Evaluate triggered pipeline execution
continuous_pipeline.why: A continuous pipeline can remain active between useful updates.
continuous_pipeline.how: Check freshness requirements and input arrival. Test triggered execution on a schedule aligned with the business SLA, and compare update duration and spend.

instance_pool_idle.title: Review warm instance pool capacity
instance_pool_idle.why: Minimum idle instances keep cloud VMs on standby. Standby VM costs are not the same as Databricks DBU costs.
instance_pool_idle.how: Review idle instance counts, minimum idle capacity and idle termination. Lower standby capacity gradually if cluster startup requirements permit.

allpurpose_shape_mismatch.title: Review all-purpose cluster shape
allpurpose_shape_mismatch.why: The balance of driver and workers may not match the measured CPU and memory bottleneck.
allpurpose_shape_mismatch.how: Inspect driver/worker evidence below. Test fewer workers, a different instance shape or single-node execution, while preserving memory and workload SLAs.

instance_generation_modernize.title: Evaluate a newer instance generation
instance_generation_modernize.why: An older instance generation may offer weaker price/performance. A newer generation is not automatically a saving.
instance_generation_modernize.how: Check regional availability and compatibility, then benchmark the suggested generation on the same workload using actual rates and duration.

warehouse_keepalive_queries.title: Review queries keeping a warehouse warm
warehouse_keepalive_queries.why: Trivial or metadata queries can prevent auto-stop without delivering meaningful workload throughput.
warehouse_keepalive_queries.how: Inspect top clients and hourly activity. Remove unnecessary keepalive polling, route metadata calls appropriately and verify that the warehouse can actually stop.

warehouse_min_clusters.title: Reduce excess minimum warehouse clusters
warehouse_min_clusters.why: A high minimum cluster count can keep capacity billed even when observed demand rarely needs more than one cluster.
warehouse_min_clusters.how: Use the staged minimum-cluster proposal below. Reduce one stage, observe peak demand, queueing and p95 runtime, then reassess before another reduction.

job_no_new_input.title: Review job runs without new input
job_no_new_input.why: Repeated scheduled runs show no new input activity. Useful side effects or sources outside lineage may not be captured.
job_no_new_input.how: Confirm ingestion and business requirements. Consider file-arrival or upstream triggers, or a less frequent schedule, while preserving required side effects.

job_task_retry_waste.title: Investigate retries inside successful jobs
job_task_retry_waste.why: Successful job runs can hide repeated failed task attempts and the compute they consumed.
job_task_retry_waste.how: Inspect task attempts, failure causes and retry policies. Fix recurring failures or skew; do not remove retries that protect reliability without an alternative.

serving_provisioned_overcapacity.title: Review provisioned serving capacity
serving_provisioned_overcapacity.why: Provisioned throughput remains allocated through hours with no observed traffic. Capacity and traffic do not establish a guaranteed saving.
serving_provisioned_overcapacity.how: Inspect the hourly traffic profile and serving requirements. Test lower or scheduled provisioned capacity where supported, monitoring throughput and latency.

unpruned_repeated_queries.title: Review repeated scans and cache misses
unpruned_repeated_queries.why: Repeated queries may scan large data volumes without effective pruning or cache reuse.
unpruned_repeated_queries.how: Inspect query plans, filters and cache behavior. Evaluate clustering, selective predicates and query reuse; benchmark changes before claiming savings.

unviewed_scheduled_dashboards.title: Review scheduled dashboards with no observed views
unviewed_scheduled_dashboards.why: Refresh schedules consume compute although no dashboard views were observed. Subscriptions and external consumers may still need the refresh.
unviewed_scheduled_dashboards.how: Confirm the owner, subscriptions and downstream use. Reduce or pause unnecessary refreshes, then verify that required delivery still works.

alert_hygiene.title: Review failing, unread or keepalive SQL alerts
alert_hygiene.why: Alert evaluations can repeatedly fail, reach no recipient or keep a warehouse warm. Alert compute may overlap warehouse findings.
alert_hygiene.how: Inspect evaluations, subscriptions and clients. Fix the query or recipients, or tune the schedule. Keep business-critical alerts; do not count overlapping savings twice.

coding_agent_smart_routing.title: Evaluate Smart Routing for coding agents
coding_agent_smart_routing.why: Coding-agent inference may be eligible for routing that uses a more appropriate model for each request.
coding_agent_smart_routing.how: Check supported clients, endpoint configuration and request evidence. Test Smart Routing and compare quality, latency and billed tokens before rollout.

sql_repeated_failures.title: Investigate repeatedly failing SQL
sql_repeated_failures.why: Repeated failed statements consume warehouse compute without producing a successful result.
sql_repeated_failures.how: Inspect recurring error signatures, query clients and failed statements. Fix or stop the source of repeated failures and validate the workload.

ai_gateway_wasted_inference.title: Investigate failed AI Gateway inference
ai_gateway_wasted_inference.why: Failed inference requests may consume billed tokens or inference capacity.
ai_gateway_wasted_inference.how: Inspect error codes, request patterns and retries. Correct authentication, payloads, limits or model configuration, then verify successful requests and billed usage.

pipeline_failed_updates.title: Investigate failed pipeline updates
pipeline_failed_updates.why: Repeated failed updates consume pipeline compute without completing the intended refresh.
pipeline_failed_updates.how: Inspect the pipeline event log and failing datasets. Fix the root cause and retry behavior, then verify a successful incremental update.

pipeline_full_refresh_churn.title: Review repeated pipeline full refreshes
pipeline_full_refresh_churn.why: Repeated full refreshes may reprocess data unnecessarily compared with an incremental update.
pipeline_full_refresh_churn.how: Inspect update triggers and reset/full-refresh settings. Confirm correctness and source semantics before switching to incremental processing.

delta_sharing_materialization.title: Review repeated Delta Sharing materialization
delta_sharing_materialization.why: Repeated materialization of shared data can consume compute and storage.
delta_sharing_materialization.how: Inspect sharing access patterns and materialization frequency. Evaluate reuse, caching and consumer requirements before changing delivery.

storage_optimization_churn.title: Review Predictive Optimization maintenance
storage_optimization_churn.why: Heavy recurring maintenance can indicate storage layout or write patterns worth investigating, not necessarily avoidable cost.
storage_optimization_churn.how: Inspect optimization history, table writes and query access. Adjust write patterns or layout only after verifying maintenance and read performance.

manual_maintenance_overlap.title: Review manual maintenance overlap
manual_maintenance_overlap.why: Manual OPTIMIZE or VACUUM may overlap Predictive Optimization, but similar operations are not proof of redundant work.
manual_maintenance_overlap.how: Compare execution history, schedules and Predictive Optimization coverage. Retire only demonstrably redundant maintenance, preserving retention requirements.

job_runaway_no_timeout.title: Set timeouts for runaway jobs
job_runaway_no_timeout.why: Abnormally long runs without a timeout can keep consuming compute.
job_runaway_no_timeout.how: Inspect historical duration and stuck runs. Set a timeout above legitimate runtime and add alerts; confirm safe cancellation and restart behavior.

idle_apps.title: App idleness cannot be inferred from lifecycle events
idle_apps.why: App deploy, start and stop events are not a request log. They cannot establish whether users are using the app.
idle_apps.how: This rule is disabled. Use the Apps inventory for observed billing and lifecycle facts; require real request telemetry before considering an idle-use recommendation.
